title: Supracondylar fracture
stem: Paediatric area. Ming, 7, fell from the monkey bars onto his outstretched left hand an hour ago. He is holding his elbow and won't let anyone move it. His mother is with him. Vital signs are normal for his age. Assess and manage.

phases.title: Opener
phases.goal: Introduce yourself, consent, and the key questions.

phases.title: Analgesia
phases.goal: Pain relief before anything moves; the elbow stays where it is comfortable.

phases.title: Neurovascular
phases.goal: Skin, then pulse, colour, warmth, refill; radial, median, AIN, ulnar; compartments.

phases.title: X-ray
phases.goal: AP and lateral in comfort; read and grade it.

phases.title: Plan
phases.goal: Orthopaedics, nil by mouth, slab no more than 90°, repeat checks, document.

phases.title: Mother
phases.goal: Explain, and tell her what to watch for.

review.text: Case. Your script is a Gartland III with a pink pulseless hand. This station keeps a Gartland II with a radial pulse and an AIN palsy, as you chose. So the 'pink pulseless is not white ischaemic' mark becomes 'states the hand is perfused with a pulse'. The other marks follow your blueprint.

Gartland II management varies: some units cast an undisplaced-looking II without wiring. Here it is angulated with a nerve palsy, so the station expects urgent orthopaedic review for reduction and pinning, and does not accept fracture clinic.
BOAST 11 (October 2020) standard numbers (1, 2, 3, 4, 8) are quoted from your script. I could not re-check them against the document here.
No public HA analgesia chart: the station says weight-based intranasal fentanyl without a dose. Add your department's dose if you want it scored.

Compartment syndrome threshold. Your notes use an absolute compartment pressure of 25 mmHg. The usual threshold is the delta pressure: diastolic pressure minus compartment pressure under 30 mmHg. The clinical signs (escalating pain, pain on passive finger extension) come first.

notes:
Checked against BOAST 11 'Supracondylar fractures of the humerus in children' (October 2020) and the Gartland classification.

X-ray: lateral view — posterior fat pad (always abnormal), elevated anterior fat pad ('sail'), anterior humeral line should pass through the middle third of the capitellum (passes anterior to it in an extension-type fracture), radiocapitellar line intact. Ossification centres CRITOE (capitellum ~1, radial head ~3, internal/medial epicondyle ~5, trochlea ~7, olecranon ~9, external/lateral epicondyle ~11 years). Gartland I undisplaced (above-elbow backslab at 90° or less, collar and cuff); II angulated with an intact posterior cortex; III completely displaced — closed reduction and K-wiring (BOAST: within 12–24 h, urgent if neurovascular compromise).

Neurovascular examination and documentation of radial, median (and anterior interosseous — 'OK' sign, FPL and FDP index), and ulnar nerves, and radial pulse and perfusion. The pink pulseless hand needs urgent orthopaedic/vascular input; the white pulseless hand is an emergency (reduce and explore). Compartment syndrome: pain out of proportion, pain on passive finger extension — early; avoid tight flexion and circumferential casts.

Your notes match this (they use a 25 mmHg compartment pressure question; the delta pressure — diastolic minus compartment under 30 mmHg — is the usual threshold).

Perfect script (essential marks): introduce, identify, consent; allergies, last meal, tetanus, mechanism, head injury; weight-based analgesia before moving, elbow in comfort; antecubital skin; colour, warmth, refill, radial pulse, both sides; radial, median, AIN, ulnar; passive stretch and compartments; AP and lateral in comfort, Gartland grade; state NV status; urgent orthopaedics, nil by mouth; slab in comfort at 90° or less, elevate, repeat NV observations; document before reduction; explain, AIN prognosis, compartment safety net. Instant fail: hyperflexing the elbow; fracture clinic for a displaced fracture; no vascular exam.

findings.pulse@wrist-R: Right radial pulse present and strong.
findings.crt@nails-R: Capillary refill 1 second on the right.
findings.stretch@pulp-L: No pain when his fingers are passively extended.
findings.compartments@forearm-L: Forearm soft, not tense; not tender to squeeze.

steps.label: Talk to his mother
steps.hint: Who you are, who he is, permission; allergies, last meal, tetanus, how he fell, head injury.

opts.t: Introduce yourself, check his name and that she is his mother, and ask to examine him
opts.tz: 你好，我係急症室醫生。你係佢媽媽？佢叫咩名？我想幫佢止痛，再睇吓隻手，可以嗎？
opts.r: Yes, I'm his mum. He's Ming. Please, he's in so much pain.
opts.rz: 係，我係佢媽媽，佢叫明仔。醫生，佢好痛呀。
opts.mark: Introduces self, identifies the child, consent to examine

opts.t: Any allergies? When did he last eat or drink? Is his tetanus up to date?
opts.tz: 佢有冇藥物敏感？最後幾點食嘢飲嘢？打齊針未？
opts.r: No allergies. He had lunch at twelve. All his injections are up to date.
opts.rz: 冇敏感。佢十二點食咗晏晝。啲針都打齊晒。
opts.mark: Asks allergies, last meal and tetanus

opts.t: How exactly did he fall? Did he hit his head?
opts.tz: 佢點樣跌㗎？有冇撞親個頭？
opts.r: He fell off the monkey bars onto his hand. He didn't hit his head and cried straight away.
opts.rz: 佢喺攀架跌落嚟，用隻手撐住。冇撞到頭，即刻喊咗出嚟。
opts.mark: Asks the mechanism and about head injury

opts.t: Let me straighten his arm so I can have a proper look
opts.tz: 等我拉直佢隻手睇清楚啲。
opts.r: He screams. Never force a painful elbow straight: give analgesia and keep it in the position of comfort.

steps.label: Talk to the nurse
steps.hint: Weight-based analgesia now, before anything is moved; keep the elbow where it is comfortable.

opts.t: Weigh him and give weight-based analgesia now (intranasal fentanyl), before anyone moves the arm
opts.r: 22 kg. Intranasal fentanyl given; he settles a little.

opts.t: Support the arm in the position he finds comfortable; nobody forces it straight or bent
opts.r: Supported on a pillow, elbow resting at about 70°.
opts.mark: Keeps the elbow in comfort; does not force flexion

opts.t: Oral paracetamol and wait to see if that helps
opts.r: Not enough for a displaced fracture in a child in severe pain.

steps.label: Neurovascular examination
steps.hint: Skin at the front of the elbow; colour, warmth, refill and radial pulse on both sides; radial, median, AIN and ulnar nerves; passive finger stretch and the forearm.

Skin.t: Front of the elbow: open wound, pucker, bruising
Skin.r: Skin intact: no puncture, no pucker. Swollen elbow with a small bruise at the front: treat the skin as threatened until orthopaedics review.
Skin.mark: Inspects the antecubital skin for an open wound or pucker

Vascular.t: Colour and warmth, compared with the other hand
Vascular.r: Both hands pink and warm, the same on each side.
Vascular.do: look hand-L & look hand-R & feel hand-L & feel hand-R

Vascular.r: Radial pulse present and strong, the same as the right.

Nerves.t: Radial nerve, motor: thumbs up and wrist back
Nerves.r: Thumbs up and wrist extension: normal.

Nerves.t: Radial nerve, sensation: back of the first web space
Nerves.r: Feels the cotton wool on the back of the first web space.

Nerves.t: Median nerve, motor: thumb to little finger
Nerves.r: Opposes the thumb to the little finger: normal.
Feels the cotton wool on the index fingertip.

Nerves.t: Anterior interosseous nerve: make an 'OK' sign
Nerves.r: A flat pinch, not a round O: he cannot bend the tip of the thumb or the index finger. Anterior interosseous nerve palsy (sensation is spared).
Nerves.mark: Tests the AIN and finds a palsy

Nerves.t: Ulnar nerve, motor: cross the fingers or spread them
Nerves.r: Crosses and spreads the fingers: normal.
Feels the cotton wool on the little finger.

Compartment.r: No pain on passive finger extension; forearm soft.

Do not.r: He screams, and the hand goes pale as the artery kinks over the fracture. Never hyperflex a supracondylar fracture: back to the position of comfort, and recheck the hand.
He screams. Forcing it straight can injure the nerve and the artery: leave it where it is comfortable.

steps.label: X-ray
steps.hint: AP and lateral of the elbow in the position of comfort; fat pads, anterior humeral line, posterior cortex.

X-ray.t: Left elbow AP and lateral, in the position of comfort
X-ray.r: Posterior fat pad and a raised anterior 'sail'. Supracondylar fracture; the anterior humeral line passes in front of the capitellum; posterior cortex intact, distal fragment angulated back: extension Gartland II.
mark: Requests AP and lateral without forcing flexion
Reads the film and grades it Gartland II

X-ray.t: Lateral with the elbow bent to 90° for a true view
X-ray.r: Forcing 90° hurts and risks the artery and nerves. Take the films in the position of comfort, even if short of 90°.
Forearm not tender: not needed this time.

steps.label: Findings
steps.hint: Perfused or not; pulse; each nerve; the skin.

opts.t: The hand is pink and warm, refill 1 second, radial pulse present: perfused, no vascular compromise
opts.mark: States the hand is perfused with a pulse

opts.t: Radial, median sensation and ulnar intact; anterior interosseous nerve palsy
opts.mark: States each nerve including the AIN palsy

opts.t: Skin intact with anterior bruising; no pain on passive stretch
opts.mark: States the skin and compartment findings

opts.t: Neurovascularly intact
opts.r: Not so: the OK sign shows an anterior interosseous nerve palsy. Sensation is spared, so it is easily missed.

steps.label: Phone orthopaedics
steps.hint: Urgent orthopaedics for reduction and pinning; nil by mouth; slab in comfort no more than 90°; repeat checks; document first.

opts.t: Orthopaedic registrar: displaced Gartland II with an AIN palsy, pink with a pulse; please review urgently for reduction and pinning today
opts.r: Coming down. Keep him nil by mouth.

opts.t: Nil by mouth
opts.r: Nurse puts a nil-by-mouth sign up.

opts.t: Above-elbow backslab in comfort, no more than 90°; sling, elevate; neurovascular observations every hour
opts.r: Slab on, elbow at about 70°; hand still pink, pulse present.
opts.mark: Backslab in comfort at 90° or less, elevate, repeat neurovascular checks

opts.t: Document the skin, pulse, refill and each nerve, including the AIN palsy, before any reduction
opts.mark: Documents the neurovascular status before reduction

opts.t: A tight full cast with the elbow fully bent
opts.r: Hyperflexion and a tight cast risk kinking the artery and compartment syndrome.

opts.t: Collar and cuff, home, fracture clinic next week
opts.r: A displaced fracture with a nerve palsy needs orthopaedics today, not fracture clinic.

opts.t: Reduce it here in ED under sedation
opts.r: Not in ED: reduction and pinning in theatre, by orthopaedics.

steps.label: Explain to his mother
steps.hint: What is broken; the nerve; the operation; what to watch for.

opts.t: The bone just above the elbow is broken and tilted; the bone doctors will straighten it and hold it with pins today
opts.tz: 佢手踭上面嗰條骨斷咗，仲歪咗。骨科醫生今日會幫佢將骨駁返正，再用鋼針固定。
opts.r: Today? Will he need an operation?
opts.mark: Explains the fracture and the plan

opts.t: The hand has good blood flow. One nerve that bends his thumb and finger tip is weak; most of these recover over weeks to months
opts.tz: 佢隻手血液循環好好。有條控制拇指同食指尾節嘅神經有啲冇力，大部分幾個禮拜到幾個月會好返。
opts.r: So it should get better by itself?
opts.mark: Explains the AIN palsy and its prognosis

opts.t: Tell the nurse at once if the pain gets worse, the fingers go pale or blue, he can't move them, or it hurts to straighten them
opts.tz: 如果佢愈嚟愈痛、手指變白或者變藍、郁唔到，或者拉直手指好痛，即刻話俾護士知。

opts.t: The nerve will definitely be back to normal
opts.r: Most recover, but you can't promise it.

qs.q: Normal anterior humeral line passes through…
qs.a: The middle third of the capitellum
wrong: In front of the whole capitellum
Through the tip of the olecranon
Through the centre of the radial head

qs.q: Nerve most often injured in extension-type supracondylar fractures?
wrong: Axillary nerve at the surgical neck

qs.a: Capitellum, Radial head, Internal epicondyle, Trochlea, Olecranon, External epicondyle
wrong: Coronoid, Radial head, Internal, Trochlea, Olecranon, External
Trochlea first, then capitellum, then radial head
Flexion type with an intact cortex

qs.q: Earliest sign of compartment syndrome in a child?
qs.a: Escalating pain, and pain on passive finger extension

qs.q: Why not flex the elbow past 90° in a backslab?
qs.a: It can kink the brachial artery and raise compartment pressure
wrong: It makes the X-ray harder to read
It stretches the ulnar nerve only

qs.q: Pink pulseless hand (perfused) after a displaced supracondylar fracture?
qs.a: Urgent reduction and pinning, then recheck; explore only if still poorly perfused

badge.name: Fat Pad
badge.flavor: Comfort, not 90°. An 'OK' for the AIN. Never cast it tight.

cards.q: A visible posterior fat pad on a lateral elbow film means…
Pink pulseless hand after supracondylar fracture needs…
options: Urgent reduction and pinning, then recheck the hand
Discharge with a collar and cuff and fracture clinic review
cards.why: Most kinked arteries recover with reduction; explore if still poorly perfused. White pulseless: emergency theatre.

options: Backslab at ≤90° and collar and cuff

cards.q: Radial head ossification appears around age…
Which four nerve functions do you document before reduction?
